summary:
Round 1 (read-only). 8e3c5fd48..ba721c3f1: fa884825 changes scripts/maintenance/demo-storage-inspect.mjs (+46/-1) and its test (+44); ba721c3f adds evidence only. The rest of the inspection script is unchanged from the version approved in #500 round 2.

Change: on a GraphQL response containing `errors`, the inspector now records state.observations.graphqlFailure = projectGraphqlFailure(body.errors) and then fails exactly as before with READONLY_GRAPHQL_REJECTED. It still fails for errors null and for an empty array. Endpoint, queries, headers, auth modes and request counts are unchanged.

Privacy and safety review of projectGraphqlFailure:
- Output is only two fixed enums:
  - errorsShape: null | empty-array | nonempty-array | malformed;
  - category: no-details | not-authorized | project-token-not-found | two-factor-required | schema-validation | rate-limited | unknown | mixed.
  No provider message, code, path, extension value or count is stored or emitted.
- Input bounds: at most 20 errors, each message a string of at most 512 characters, plain objects only, extensions.code a string of at most 64 characters; anything else is reported as malformed/unknown.
- Classification: an extension code is matched against a fixed allowlist (UNAUTHENTICATED/FORBIDDEN→not-authorized, GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED/GRAPHQL_PARSE_FAILED→schema-validation, RATE_LIMITED/TOO_MANY_REQUESTS→rate-limited, else unknown). Otherwise the message is compared by exact lowercase equality ('project token not found', 'not authorized', 'two factor authentication required') or an anchored schema-error prefix. The message is only compared, never copied.
- The observation is set before the constant-code failure, so it reaches the receipt only as these enums. No secret, token or clinical data can enter it.

Tests: the null, empty, malformed, oversized, per-code, per-message, mixed and unknown cases each assert the exact enum pair and that the original provider strings do not appear in the receipt output.

CI on ba721c3f1: test, gate, secret-scan, frontend-tests, browser-e2e, archive-tests, bug-pipeline-tests, real-provider, windows-review-setup and Vercel all pass. inspect, configure-repository and verify-provider-access are skipped by design (dispatch-only).

Limit: synthetic evidence only; the real classification of Railway's responses will be seen on the next real dispatch. Read with git (blobless clone); no PR code or tests were run by the reviewer.
